prompt: A voice assistant understands most users but often fails for people with strong regional accents or speech impairments.
tells: strong regional accents or speech impairments
why: Designing so everyone can use it, including people with impairments, is inclusiveness.
trap: Fairness is about unequal decisions; this is people being unable to use it.

prompt: A new AI app can only be used by dragging on images, so blind users relying on screen readers are locked out.
tells: blind users relying on screen readers are locked out
why: Accessibility for people with disabilities is inclusiveness.
trap: Nobody is being scored differently; they simply can't use it.

prompt: The team invites deaf users and non-native speakers to help design and test a captioning tool from the start.
tells: deaf users and non-native speakers to help design
why: Involving diverse users in design is how inclusiveness is put into practice.
trap: They're shaping the design, not checking outcome rates.

prompt: An AI tutor needs fast internet and a new phone, so students in rural areas with older devices can't use it.
tells: students in rural areas with older devices can't use it
why: Leaving groups unable to benefit is an inclusiveness issue.
trap: A small model might be a fix, but the principle asked about is inclusiveness.

prompt: A video-call assistant adds support for users who communicate in sign language.
why: Designing for people with disabilities is inclusiveness.

prompt: An AI benefits assistant rewrites its answers in plain language because many applicants have limited literacy.
why: Making the system usable by people with different abilities is inclusiveness.

prompt: An AI writing helper adds a mode with simpler layouts and read-aloud for users with dyslexia.
